379YE Winter Solstice Imperial elections.d: Ten territories were due to appoint senators, each by its own national custom, from Dawn's Tourney for Astolat to the largest purse for Madruga. Skarsind was to elect the first Imperial Orc senator. Generals were due for seven armies and an admiral for the Brass Coast navy, chosen unanimously by national senators or else by the Senate. The orc tradition of choosing generals by contest in the fighting pit was expected to face scrutiny. The Synod was to fill Cardinals of the Way and Prosperity, the Conscience of the Senate, the High Exorcist and the Voice of Barbs. The Bourse had five weirwood seats at auction, the Senate was to decide the Vigilant Swan's allocation, and several national ministries were open.

n.Dawn: Dawnish nobles whose houses held no Senate seat could compete in the Tourney for Astolat's seat, and the generalship of the Hounds of Glory was also to be filled.
n.Highguard: Chapters in Necropolis could put forward candidates for the Highborn senator, chosen by citizens with congregations.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were to elect their first ever senator, for Skarsind, and the Winter Sun needed a general, though the custom of choosing generals in the fighting pit was expected to come under scrutiny now the orcs had a senator.
n.Navarr: The Navarr were to elect a senator for Hercynia in an open-air vote, appoint the Voice of Barbs through their national assembly, and choose the holder of the Thimble from among herb garden holders.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn dhomiro could bid for the right to appoint Madruga's senator, an admiral was needed for the Freeborn navy, and fleet captains were to choose the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills.
n.The League: Temeschwari business owners were to back candidates for their senator, and the Towerjacks needed a general.
n.The Marches: Bregasland farm owners were to align with stewards to name their senator, the Strong Reeds needed a general, and Marcher farmers could vote for the Bailiff of the Grand Market.
n.Urizen: Zenith's spires could put up candidates for senator, voted on by the territory's ritual magicians, while Urizen mana site owners were to choose the Provost of the Halls of Knowledge.
n.Varushka: Any Varushkan could stand for Miekarova's seat, with the wise ones judging the wisest candidate, and the Army of the Golden Axe needed a general.
n.Wintermark: Any Wintermark citizen could stand for Kallavesa's seat, decided by the Kallavesi alone, and the Green Shield Army needed a general.

t.Astolat: Astolat's senator was to be decided by a Tourney open to nobles whose houses did not already hold a Senate seat.
t.Bregasland: Marchers owning farms in Bregasland were to align with stewards to compete for the right to name the territory's senator.
t.Hercynia: Any Navarr could stand for Hercynia's seat, but only those with resources in Hercynia could vote in the open-air election.
t.Kahraman: The Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills, chosen by Freeborn fleet captains, would take responsibility for looking after Kahraman along with the right to buy trade goods.
t.Kallavesa: Only the Kallavesi were to have a say in who would represent their marshy territory in the Senate.
t.Madruga: The Freeborn dhomiro who put in the largest purse would claim the right to appoint Madruga's senator.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova's senator was to be the candidate the wise ones judged the wisest.
t.Necropolis: Chapters in Necropolis could each put forward a candidate for senator, with Highborn citizens holding congregations selecting the best.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was to elect the first Imperial Orc senator at this Solstice.
t.Temeschwar: Citizens running businesses in Temeschwar were to throw their weight behind their favoured candidate for senator.
t.Zenith: Each spire in Zenith could put forward a candidate, with the territory's ritual magicians voting on who would represent them.

379YE Winter Solstice Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 1534 thrones and 4 crowns, with no donations. Passed motions included creating the Seer of the Gateway, Trade Envoy to the Sarcophan Delves and Civilian Commissioners titles, constructing a mithril mine, the Tassato Mana Exchange, Mines of Gulhule, Torfast Trading Post and a shrine to Britta, fortifying the Ore Hills, raising the Imperial Guerdon and declaring war on the Barrens orcs. A disbursement to Senator Sarvos failed and the Ministry for Jarmish Slaves was withdrawn. The civil service asked whether the Brilliant Shore seat, held by the Steinr Joakim, should be reappointed by the Imperial Orcs now or remain with him until Summer 380YE or his death.

n.Imperial Orcs: With Skarsind now theirs, the Brilliant Shore automatically became an Imperial Orc national bourse seat, though the civil service asked the Senate whether the orcs should reappoint it this Solstice or leave it with its current holder.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark lost the Brilliant Shore as a national bourse resource with Skarsind's transfer, though the Steinr Joakim still held the seat pending the Senate's advice on whether he keeps it until Summer 380YE or his death.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind's change of hands to the Imperial Orcs created an unprecedented question over its Brilliant Shore bourse seat, which the civil service referred to the Senate.

379YE Winter Solstice winds of fortune.d: The Senate's decision to relinquish Skarsind was ratified and the territory assigned to the Imperial Orcs, while Thane Dogri Thulebane claimed Crow's Ridge for Wintermark. Reikos was liberated. Curses blighted the Marcher harvest and Bastion, and a Summer enchantment settled over Varushka. Vigilance launched a crusade against the vyig. Druj, Thule, Grendel and Barrens orc delegations headed to Anvil. The Iron Confederacy finished conquering Kalino and sought a treaty. The Hierro camped near Anduz, and Britta's regalia was interred in Kallavesa. Opportunities included a Dawnish crusade on Dawnguard and a northern discovery. In Karsk the Thule withdrew, road rebuilding began, but no progress was made on mustering the Iron Helm.

n.Dawn: Troubadours urged Dawn to raise a fourth army and launch a major assault on Dawnguard and the Towers of the Dawn to conquer the Barrens; this was presented as an opportunity, not an action taken.
n.Druj: The Druj sent a delegation to Anvil and had been driven out of Holberg, though their legacy of ruins, marshes and killer trees remained there.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel delegation was among the barbarian orcs travelling to Anvil for the Solstice.
n.Highguard: Highguard saw Reikos liberated and a preacher named Golan rise there, while a curse of hail, sleet and doubt struck at the faith of Bastion and Britta's regalia left the Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Senate assigned Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs as their homeland, uniting the nation in one place for the first time. However, Winterfolk under Dogri Thulebane claimed Crow's Ridge, and groups of ambitious bonesetters offered the orcs opportunities.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Hearth Tithe herbs grown in the Marches and Wintermark were intended to help the war against the Jotun.
n.The Brass Coast: The Hierro clan camped near Anduz in Segura, and a magical wind across four Freeborn territories summoned the hakima and the Kohan to a council.
n.The League: The Vigilance assembly launched a crusade against the vyig in Temeschwar, Tassato and Holberg, and Holberg continued to suffer the aftermath of Druj occupation.
n.The Marches: Serious curses devastated the Autumn harvest across Upwold, Mitwold and Bregasland, threatening military supplies and food prices. Marcher farms also set aside land for the Hearth Tithe, and peculiar births occurred near King's Stoke.
n.Thule: The Thule withdrew from most of Karsk under the peace treaty, received the Silver Peaks, and sent a delegation to Anvil.
n.Urizen: Urizen made its decision on how to use a trove of mage weapons and armour found beneath the Unmade Spire in Redoubt.
n.Varushka: A powerful Summer enchantment settled over the whole of Varushka. Meanwhile the Golden Axe reassured Karsk, roads were rebuilt, and colleges began construction in Volchitrava and Mieriada.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's pride festered over the surrender of the Silver Peaks, and Dogri Thulebane claimed Crow's Ridge for the nation. The Hearth Tithe was reintroduced, Britta's regalia was interred in Kallavesa, and a far-northern discovery offered an opportunity.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page refers only to a possible fourth army being raised in Dawn for a crusade.
t.Bastion: An insidious curse of hail, sleet and a malign aura encouraging doubt in faith lay over Bastion for three months.
t.Bregasland: Curses devastated Bregasland's Autumn harvest as part of the attack on the Marches' farms.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named directly on this page.
t.Feroz: A magical wind blew across Feroz calling the hakima and the Kohan to a council.
t.Holberg: Holberg was a target of Vigilance's crusade against the vyig, and the Druj legacy of ruins, spreading marshes and killer trees lingered after their expulsion.
t.Kahraman: A magical wind blew across Kahraman calling the hakima and the Kohan to a council.
t.Kalino: The Iron Confederacy had apparently finished conquering Kalino from the Lasambrians, giving them a land border with the Empire.
t.Kallavesa: The regalia of Empress Britta was interred alongside her body in the marshes of Kallavesa.
t.Karsk: Thule forces withdrew to the north-eastern hills under the peace treaty, and Senate-approved road rebuilding began. However, no progress was made on mustering the Iron Helm.
t.Madruga: A magical wind blew across Madruga calling the hakima and the Kohan to a council.
t.Miekarova: Construction began in Miekarova's Mieriada region on the Hearth of the Tempest, intended to aid the exploration of Spring magic.
t.Mitwold: Curses devastated Mitwold's Autumn harvest, damaging the Marches' farms.
t.Necropolis: The regalia of Empress Britta was removed from her shrine in the Necropolis and taken to Kallavesa.
t.Redoubt: Urizen decided how to use the trove of mage weapons and armour found beneath the Unmade Spire in Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Reikos was liberated and became Imperial territory again, though some barbarian orcs remained. The preacher Golan began calling there for Courage to be recognised as the most fundamental virtue.
t.Segura: Orcs of the Hierro clan camped close to the walls of Anduz, and Segura also felt the magical wind summoning the hakima and the Kohan.
t.Sermersuaq: The surrender of Sermersuaq's Silver Peaks to the Thule left a festering wound in Wintermark's pride.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was assigned to the Imperial Orcs, but Dogri Thulebane's Winterfolk followers seized Crow's Keep and claimed Crow's Ridge for Wintermark.
t.Tassato: Tassato was a target of Vigilance's crusade against the vyig.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar was a target of Vigilance's crusade against the vyig.
t.The Barrens: Dawnish troubadours called for a major assault to conquer the Barrens, and the independent Barrens orcs sent a delegation to Anvil.
t.Upwold: Curses devastated Upwold's harvest, and peculiar births were reported near King's Stoke.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: The ruins of Holmauer remained as part of the Druj legacy in Holberg.
r.Holberg/The Morass: Mentioned in passing: the page refers generally to spreading marshes left by the Druj in Holberg.
r.Karsk/Branoc: The Golden Axe swept through Branoc, reassuring the Varushkan people that the orcs had gone.
r.Karsk/Crowslook: The Golden Axe swept through Crowslook, reassuring the Varushkan people that the orcs had gone.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Under the peace treaty, the Thule withdrew their Karsk forces to the north-eastern hills of Krevstay.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: The miners of Moresvah offered aid towards restoring the Iron Helm, but no progress had been made on mustering it.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Construction began in Mieriada on the Hearth of the Tempest, intended to aid the exploration of Spring magic.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: Mentioned in passing: the page names the Unmade Spire in Redoubt, where the trove was found, but does not name Tomari.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Silver Peaks had been surrendered to the Thule, a loss that continued to wound Wintermark's pride.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Thane Dogri Thulebane declared Crow's Ridge part of Wintermark, and his followers took Crow's Keep as their base and drew in disgruntled Winterfolk.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Dawnguard and the Towers of the Dawn were the proposed target of a major Dawnish crusade.
r.Upwold/Tower March: Half a dozen very peculiar births occurred near the town of King's Stoke in Tower March.

379YE Winter Solstice winds of war.d: A magical Spring storm levelled Fort Mezudan, killing seventy including Illuminate Nissea, before Imperial armies pushed the Grendel out of Ateri. With Urith Barath fallen, Dawnish and Navarr armies swept Longshire and Broken Ride, freeing slaves and making Reikos Imperial again, though orcs linger in Tamarbode and Grey Charge. Rahvin-led Barrens orcs badly damaged the Towers of the Dawn. Freeborn armies were roughly halfway to taking Liath's Ring, but around forty thousand Jotun overran Western Scout and Beacon Point, slaughtering Navarr and leaving all of Liathaven in Jotun hands. In the Mournwold, Marcher, Imperial Orc and Highborn armies retook the Ore Hills with an unfinished Jotun fortress and advanced into Freemoor.

n.Dawn: The Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky crushed the orcs of Longshire and helped clear Exile, but at home the Rahvin-led Barrens orcs left the Towers of the Dawn badly damaged and Dawnguard under threat.
n.Druj: The Stone Toad clan was broken and scattered after the fall of Urith Barath, losing Reikos save for scattered remnants in Tamarbode, Grey Charge and the Great Forest.
n.Grendel: Grendel sorcery destroyed Fort Mezudan, but their armies lost perhaps three thousand orcs and were pushed out of Ateri, withdrawing in good order to Apulus and Screed while gathering mana and metal.
n.Highguard: Highborn chapter banners flew once more over Chalcis Mount as Reikos returned to Imperial hands, though the territory lies ruined and much of its population is dead or exiled; Highborn armies also fought in Spiral and the Mournwold.
n.Imperial Orcs: Both Imperial Orc armies joined the Mournwold offensive, the Summer Storm and Winter Sun helping take the Ore Hills before pushing north into Freemoor.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost the Ore Hills and their unfinished fortress and fell back in Freemoor, but a vast force conquered southern Liathaven, giving them control of every region there.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns liberated Broken Ride and around a hundred and fifty slaves, but the Navarr of southern Liathaven were butchered by the Jotun, with survivors fleeing or hiding.
n.The Brass Coast: The Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South pushed into northern Liathaven and were around halfway to taking Liath's Ring, poised to besiege Mournstead, as the Corsairs' husks finally collapsed.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South marched through Tassato, and the Mournwold advance may eventually shield Tassato from the Jotun.
n.The Marches: The Tusks and Bounders led the first Marcher advance into the Mournwold in a generation, retaking the Ore Hills, facing human collaborators and gaining a handful of local Marcher rebels in Freemoor.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the peace treaty with the Thule appeared to be holding.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost Fort Mezudan and seventy people, including Illuminate Nissea and most of the stone-crafters guild, though Ateri was retaken and Urizeni tacticians estimate six months to conquer Screed.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched south out of Wintermark, and Wintermark sellswords fought with the Wolves of War in Spiral.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: named as one place the remaining Reikos orcs cannot hope to escape to.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the two Brass Coast armies joined forces here before pushing out of the marshes into Liathaven.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: named as a possible refuge for fleeing Reikos orcs and a possible route for any new threat to Reikos.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Sentinel waits there should Reikos orcs flee west.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South marched north up the coast from Feroz.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun fort of Hillstop watches the approach from Kahraman, and Navarr survivors from Liathaven may try to flee through its bandit-haunted mountains.
t.Liathaven: The Freeborn made slow progress in the north, but the Jotun conquered the south, butchered Navarr steadings and now control every region, with the vallorn dividing the two fronts.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: home to Marcher exiles who fled the Mournwold.
t.Mournwold: Imperial armies began liberating the territory, retaking the Ore Hills and nearly half of Freemoor, while Orchard's Watch was completed in Greensward opposite the Jotun castle in Southmoor.
t.Reikos: Reikos is Imperial again after Longshire and Broken Ride were liberated and magical rain cleansed the Flux, though the land is ruined, the miasma lingers and the Senate must assign it.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: part of the Jotun host that invaded southern Liathaven came north out of the hills of Reinos.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: cited as an example of how costly a committed barbarian force can make reconquest.
t.Spiral: Fort Mezudan was destroyed by a Spring storm, but Imperial armies retook Ateri; the rest of Spiral remains firmly in Grendel hands.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South passed through, and the Mournwold campaign aims to place a barrier between the Jotun and the city.
t.The Barrens: The independent Barrens orcs, led by the Rahvin, launched a renewed assault from the wilds on Dawnguard, badly damaging the Towers of the Dawn while largely sparing civilians.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: home to Marcher exiles who fled the Mournwold.

r.Liathaven/Beacon Point: The Jotun took the region, and the Southern Bear burnt its fortified steading to the ground after a two-day siege.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Heart: Mentioned in passing: one of the vallorn-infested regions that any force must pass through to cross between northern and southern Liathaven.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: The Freeborn armies are a little over halfway to taking the region and nearly ready to besiege the Jotun supply fort of Mournstead.
r.Liathaven/Western Scout: A huge Jotun force overran the region, capturing or burning steadings and killing the Navarr they caught.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Mentioned in passing: one of the vallorn-infested regions that any force must pass through to cross between northern and southern Liathaven.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: The Tusks and Imperial Orcs freed a little under half the region against strong resistance, joined by around two-score local Marcher rebels.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: The Imperial armies massed at Overton to launch the liberation, and Orchard's Watch was completed here as the Solstice began.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Liberated after a brutal two-day battle; the captured, damaged Jotun fortress could be finished in six months for forty white granite and ten Thrones.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: The region remains in Jotun hands, anchored by their white granite castle Hillstop in the ruins of Sarcombe, now mirrored by Orchard's Watch.
r.Reikos/Broken Ride: The Black Thorns destroyed the fleeing Druj and freed around a hundred and fifty slaves, though the overseer burnt the weirwood harvest; Dawn and Navarr then cleared the defiled ruins of Exile.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: With Urith Barath torn down, High Chalcis was retaken and Highborn chapter banners were raised over the shattered ruin.
r.Reikos/Grey Charge: Still technically under orc control, but its orcs are scattered and weak with nowhere to flee.
r.Reikos/Longshire: The Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky overwhelmed the region's scattered brigand orcs and swept it clean.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Still technically under orc control, but its orcs are scattered and weak with nowhere to flee.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Most of the retreating Grendel withdrew here, likely to draw on supplies from their naval forces.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Imperial armies drove the Grendel out over three months of bitter fighting, inflicting around three thousand casualties.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Mentioned in passing: the Empire made no headway towards the Legacy in Ossuary, seen perhaps only by Quiet Step scouts.
r.Spiral/Screed: About a third of the retreating Grendel dug in around Screed, which Urizeni tacticians estimate could take six months to conquer near the Black Plateau.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Barrens orcs besieged the Towers of the Dawn and raided manor houses, leaving the towers below half strength as the only bar to the region's swift conquest.

A fine and private place.d: The new regio counts as a strong Winter regio but cannot target rituals beyond its own territory. Those who linger there take on draughir-like thoughts. From the fourth hour of the afternoon until midnight on the Saturday of the Winter Solstice, its portal led to a Winter Chamber that Tharim and the other Winter eternals declared neutral ground. There they would grant each prepared boon to whichever nation offered the most dragonbone. Until Sunday sunrise the Imperial regio lost its Winter component entirely. The heralds addressed many nations, most of them long gone. Tharim's heralds revealed the winners before the Spring Equinox 380YE.

n.Dawn: The royal houses of the Dawn were among the peoples Tharim's heralds named, inviting them to choose a representative to offer dragonbone tribute in the Winter Chamber for the eternals' boons.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the travelling actors recalled reducing the dour Highborn of Necropolis to tears of laughter during an earlier performance.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: news of the battle for the Mournwold was beginning to reach the Marches as the actors performed.

t.Casinea: The new Winter regio appeared at Anvil in Casinea. Winter rituals performed there were strengthened but could target only Casinea, and its portal to the Winter Chamber was open for one night of the Winter Solstice.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the first stories of the battle for the Mournwold were filtering north to the Marches at the time.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the mummer troupe had once performed their comedy in Necropolis to great acclaim.

A heap of broken images.d: Synod missionaries restored the Hierro's Ambition, Courage and Pride, but the orcs bent the Virtues to excuse raiding and mocked the Labyrinth. The Senate paid them 75 thrones a season, and they asked for 100 mithril or weirwood to rebuild an army of fewer than three thousand fighting-fit orcs. They demanded admission as an eleventh nation with their own homeland, Madruga or Segura, and offered to conquer one if needed. The General Assembly backed Duke Ferrero, who quelled Seguran tensions for the season but could not secure resupply. It also backed Elka Nadyanova Gremani, who drew the Hierro towards orthodoxy with 100 liao. A third judgement inviting them to Holmauer, made without liao, had no effect.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: level-headed Freeborn suggested Reikos, then held by Highguard and up for allocation, as a distant homeland for the Hierro, though it cannot legally be given to foreigners.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Hierro refused point-blank to join the Imperial Orcs, yet cited their homeland as a precedent. Freeborn fears drew on the Senate's earlier transfer of Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs.
n.Jotun: The Hierro named the Jotun to the west as a threat to their exposed camp in south-western Segura, and promised to reclaim Jotun-held Reinos if they became an Imperial nation.
n.Navarr: The Navarr priest Taryn of Exile's End led the Synod's missionary work among the Hierro. His teaching revived their spirit but also produced near-heretical interpretations of the Virtues.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn in Segura and Madruga were alarmed that the Hierro demanded one of their territories as a homeland, and some talked of driving them out. Duke Ferrero's preaching kept the peace in Segura for the season.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn compared Hierro honesty unfavourably to a 'League mountebank', and an unfunded judgement invited the Hierro to visit Holmauer in Holberg.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Freeborn cited the Senate taking Skarsind from Wintermark for the Imperial Orcs as a reason to fear losing Segura.

t.Holberg: A General Assembly judgement urged the Hierro to visit Holmauer in Holberg to see more of the Empire, but without liao behind it, it had no immediate effect.
t.Kalino: Mentioned in passing: the Hierro declared they would recover Kalino, then held by the Iron Confederacy, for their new nation if admitted to the Empire.
t.Madruga: The Hierro named Madruga as their preferred homeland because it does not border their enemies, and offered to conquer it if that helped. Locals who knew of the demand were far from pleased.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: some Freeborn suggested Reikos as a distant homeland for the Hierro, though assigning it to foreigners is not legal.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Hierro listed Reinos, held by the Jotun, among the lost territories they would reclaim once established in the Empire.
t.Segura: The Hierro camp south of Anduz grew more permanent as tensions with Freeborn farmers mounted. Duke Ferrero's liao-backed preaching of tolerance quelled the troubles for the Winter, but not enough to let the orcs resupply.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the earlier transfer of Skarsind from Wintermark to the Imperial Orcs was cited by worried Freeborn as a precedent for losing Segura.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: An unfunded Synod judgement invited the Hierro to come to Holmauer to marvel at its agriculture and wildlife, but it had no immediate effect.

A job worth doing.d: Before the Autumn Equinox a powerful Winter curse had raised the Castle of Thorns' upkeep and damaged its structure. Shortly afterwards, koboldi emissaries of King Adamant, summoned by the Spire of the Auric Horizon, appeared overnight. Supernaturally strong, resilient and swift expert masons and engineers, they repaired all structural damage and many minor faults within two days, then departed. The castle was left at full strength and in its best repair since completion. Dawnish enchanters confirmed the koboldi were intelligent Summer beings. Their chief engineer said King Adamant, who admires impressive stonework, would likely send emissaries, and asked about the Conclave and archmages. At the Winter Solstice koboldi visited Anvil, encouraging fortification-building and asking about mines.

n.Dawn: Dawn's great fortress was fully restored at no apparent cost to its people, and Dawnish enchanters gained first-hand knowledge of King Adamant's servants and the eternal's admiration for grand stone structures like the Castle of Thorns.

t.Astolat: The Castle of Thorns in Astolat was cleansed of every lingering effect of the Winter curse and left cleaner and in better repair than at any time since it was completed, after koboldi workers swarmed its walls and thorny battlements for two days.

A long good-bye.d: Following the Sarvos raids, three priests named by the Synod rallied citizens, militia and magistrates against the vyig. Vladimir von Temeschwar led the effort in Holberg, Valimir von Temeschwar in Tassato and Irada von Temeschwar in Temeschwar, where the vyig fought back with arms and fire. Their operations in Tassato and Holberg were ended, and their Temeschwar ring was smashed. The leader Bollek was believed dead, though questions remained about his fate. The upheaval reduced business income in the four cities by a quarter. Five confiscated vyig assets were to be auctioned at the Winter Solstice, but bad weather prevented this and the auction was rescheduled for Spring 380YE.

n.Dawn: Several dozen Dawnish questing knights and knights-errant joined the sweep of Holberg alongside Vladimir von Temeschwar.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the vyig are said to have mostly deserted Holberg during the earlier Druj siege.
n.Navarr: Wily Navarr thorns helped uncover a trade in stolen goods passing between Mestra and Regario in Tassato.
n.The League: League citizens led the fight against the vyig in their cities, freeing Holberg and Tassato of the criminals and smashing their Temeschwar operations, at the cost of a quarter of their business income for the season.
n.Varushka: Varushkan schlacta and volhov joined the hunt for vyig in Temeschwar, and goods stolen from Varushka were found being smuggled south through Bartelli's Bolt.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: goods stolen from Wintermark were among those smuggled through Bartelli's Bolt for sale to overseas buyers.

t.Holberg: Holberg was searched with help from orc thief-takers and Dawnish knights, ending vyig operations there, and the seized Tunnel Snakes smuggling network was earmarked for sale to an honest owner.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the summer raids in Sarvos are named as the start of the campaign, and the opening story tells of a vyig Uncle driven out of the city.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: thief-takers from the Imperial orc camp at Estcastle came to help hunt the vyig in Holberg.
t.Tassato: Valimir von Temeschwar brokered a temporary truce between rival Princes, and by winter the vyig were no longer a force in the twin city, though Callista di Tassato Regario and several allies died in the fight.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar saw a week of open battles in the city and nearby forests, weapon caches and plans for insurrection were uncovered, and the vyig ring was smashed with help from the Vardstein Voyi bravos.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Several armed clashes took place in the ruins of Holmauer, where the vyig had been trying to build criminal dens among the rubble.
r.Semmerholm/Estmure: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial orc camp at Estcastle sent thief-takers to help in Holberg.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: The vyig enforcers of Auntie Vivian fled Mestra after murdering Uncle Uzo, and the merrow Carta de Fimi Nacoso, forced into ferrying stolen goods after its head was blackmailed, was seized for auction.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Pressing Matters, a Regario printworks secretly used by confidence tricksters who had tried to counterfeit Bourse certificates, was seized, and Regario lost Callista di Tassato Regario of the Charitable Chain of Andromeo.
r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: The militia shut down Auntie Bimber's Palinka, a Hanuri tavern used as neutral ground by vyig factions, and offered its largely intact premises for auction.
r.Temeschwar/Locul: Mentioned in passing: Locul is not named directly and is covered only as part of the wider Temeschwar campaign.

Allocate Great Pits of Ennerlund.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by the senator for Therunin, the motion passed. The Great Pits of Ennerlund, a mithril mine wrecked by the Druj, were under repair at the time. Repairs were expected to be finished after the Summer Solstice 380YE, with the first mithril reaching the holder of the seat at the Autumn Equinox 380YE. The bourse seat tied to the Pits was to be auctioned at that same Autumn Equinox 380YE, opening the restored mine's output to whoever won the position.

n.Druj: The Druj are named as having destroyed the Great Pits of Ennerlund, the damage that made the repairs and this allocation necessary.
n.The League: The League's Holberg senator proposed the motion, which secured the restored mithril mine in League-held Holberg as an Imperial bourse seat to be auctioned at the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

t.Holberg: Holberg's Great Pits of Ennerlund were set to become an Imperial bourse position once repairs to the mine were finished after the Summer Solstice 380YE.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Ennerlund is home to the Great Pits, which were being rebuilt after Druj destruction and were expected to yield their first mithril for the new bourse seat at the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

Assignment of Reikos.d: The motion to assign Reikos as an Imperial territory was proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by the senator for Casinea. It passed, and Reikos was assigned to Highguard. As a result, Reikos became entitled to elect its own senator to sit in the Imperial Senate.

n.Highguard: Highguard gained Reikos as one of its territories, with the motion proposed and seconded by the Highborn senators for Necropolis and Casinea.

t.Reikos: Reikos was formally assigned to Highguard as an Imperial territory and became able to elect a senator of its own.

Black and white.d: While searching for troll artefacts, Peter of Hintown's party found unworked mithril near where the glacier meets the sea, and experts confirmed a significant deposit. Exploiting it needed a Senate motion: 100 Thrones for a mine producing 10 wains a season, or 200 Thrones for deeper workings producing 15. The find would create a Bourse seat, either Imperial or national to Wintermark. Advisers warned that the site lies close to Jotun and Thule lands and to whatever might emerge from Tsirku or the glacier, and urged a fortification. At the Winter Solstice Senator Atte provided 200 Thrones and work began, with completion projected for Autumn 380YE. No fortification was built. Prospectors were sent in Spring 382YE.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: a Winterfolk expedition member grumbles that the Senate might take the find away and give it to the orcs.
n.Jotun: The Empire was already at war with the Jotun, and the mine's closeness to Jotun lands was named as a serious threat to the new resource.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the discoverer, Peter of Hintown, is a Marcher who longs to be back home in Bregasland.
n.Thule: The mine lies close to Thule lands and would come under immediate threat if hostilities with the Thule were renewed. Peter is also investigating a possible link between the Thule invasion and the trolls.
n.Wintermark: The mithril was found in Wintermark's Sermersuaq, so a national Bourse seat would fall to Wintermark, normally appointed by its captains. Senator Atte funded the mine's construction.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Peter of Hintown remembers its Feni-haunted drowned ruins with unexpected nostalgia.
t.Sermersuaq: A significant mithril deposit was found at the Face of Ikka, and the Senate commissioned a 200-Throne mine there, projected to be ready by Autumn 380YE.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page; the only link is an expedition member's fear that the find might be handed to the orcs.
t.Tsirku: The mithril find lies on the glacier border between Tsirku and the Empire, and any horror emerging from Tsirku would likely fall straight on the mine.

r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The new mithril mine is being built on the edge of Suaq Fount. Advisers urged a fortification there to protect it and the Face of Ikka artefacts, but none was commissioned.

Clarification on the Brilliant Shore.d: In Winter 379YE an administrative motion asked the Senate to clarify the status of the Brilliant Shore, a national bourse resource in Skarsind. The question was whether the position should remain with the current seat holder until next up for election, or pass immediately to the Imperial Orcs to elect. The Senate decided the seat should remain with the current holder. As a result, the Brilliant Shore bourse seat would become available for election by the Imperial Orcs at the Summer Solstice 380YE.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were not given the Brilliant Shore seat at once, but gained the right to elect its holder at the Summer Solstice 380YE.

t.Skarsind: The Brilliant Shore, a bourse resource in Skarsind, kept its current seat holder until the Imperial Orcs could elect a new one at the Summer Solstice 380YE.

Construct College of the Liberated.d: Proposed by Casinea and seconded by Sarvos, with wording help from Senator Miaren, the motion passed at 100 thrones and 4 crowns, disbursed to Senator Casinea. Ferrero Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato supplied 40 wains of white granite and 10 thrones after the Winter Solstice. The College was built in the town of Trivento and, once complete, enhances the earnings of Sarvos businesses whose owners attended the previous Anvil summit. The Constitutional Court found it legal, provided the Jarmish newcomers are told they need not stay or study there; spare places could go to Sarvos orphans and poor. The Senate appoints the Dean of the Liberated for life.

n.The League: A League senator proposed the College and a League merchant supplied its materials, giving the League a new Senate-appointed title and greater prosperity for Sarvos businesses whose owners attended the Anvil summit.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos gained the College of the Liberated in Trivento, which educates willing former Jarmish slaves and could also take in local orphans and poor, while boosting the earnings of eligible Sarvos businesses.

r.Sarvos/Bocche: The map places the College here; the page records it as built in the town of Trivento, where former Jarmish slaves may receive education and apprenticeships.

Construct Glen of Shadows Trading Office.d: The motion followed an earlier one to establish a trading post in the town of Torfast, and formed part of an opportunity to improve the wealth of Skarsind. It passed in principle and was then approved at 22 thrones, which were disbursed to the senator for Hercynia. Construction needed 8 wains of white granite, 2 thrones in labour and three months of work. Cenwyn Thorntarry provided the granite and labour costs after the Spring Equinox 380YE. The resulting ministry created a new Imperial title, the Broker of Treji Wayhouse, able to purchase trade goods. The motion lacked some necessary details, which the senator could decide.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs stood to gain from the new office, which was meant to ease trade with their people in Skarsind and improve the territory's wealth.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind was the intended beneficiary: the office in neighbouring Hercynia supported trade with it, following on from the planned trading post at Torfast, as part of an opportunity to improve the territory's wealth.

Construct Golden Orchards of Miaren.d: Proposed by Therunin and seconded by Sarvos, the motion created a sinecure in Miaren that produces mana crystals. Its holder is appointed for life by unanimous decision of the Navarri Senators. The motion passed at 30 thrones, and the senator was left to decide the size of the sinecure. The 30 thrones were disbursed to Senator Therunin, and Caerwyn provided 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns. The Golden Orchards were completed, creating the Navarri national position of Granger of the Golden Orchard.

n.Navarr: Navarr gained a new national position, the Granger of the Golden Orchard, a lifetime post appointed by unanimous decision of the Navarri Senators that controls a source of mana crystals.

t.Miaren: The Golden Orchards were built in Miaren near Seren, giving the territory a sinecure that produces mana crystals.

Construct Mines of Gulhule.d: Proposed by Feroz and seconded by the Senator for Skarsind, the motion answered an opportunity to develop the mines of Gulhule. Three funding options were offered: 6 wains of mithril with 12 crowns plus a 12-crown outlay for green iron and orichalcum; 8 wains and 16 crowns plus 16 for those and tempest jade; or 10 wains and 20 crowns plus 20 for those, weltsilver and potentially more valuable materials. After the Winter Solstice Yargol supplied 10 wains of mithril and 40 crowns, the largest option. The work was completed, creating the Imperial title of Foreman of the Mines of Gulhule.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs gained a ministry through which they can buy ingots, including green iron, orichalcum, tempest jade and weltsilver, funded by Yargol and overseen by the new Foreman of the Mines of Gulhule.

t.Skarsind: The Mines of Gulhule were built in Skarsind to organise its miners, giving the territory a major new ministry and the Imperial title of Foreman of the Mines of Gulhule.

Construct Pilgrim's Trail.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Karov. It was passed in principle and passed at 60 thrones, which were disbursed to the senator for Kallavesa. The great work was costed at 30 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood and 10 thrones in labour, and would take three months to construct. It was described as an opportunity to draw pilgrims to Kallavesa. After the Spring Equinox 380YE, Olle Markusson provided the granite, weirwood and thrones, and the Pilgrim's Trail was completed.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a completed great work in one of its territories, with Olle Markusson supplying the granite, weirwood and thrones needed to finish the Pilgrim's Trail.

t.Kallavesa: A network of roads was built through Kallavesa to help pilgrims travel, with the aim of raising attendance at the territory's congregations and drawing pilgrims there.

Construct Torfast Trading Post.d: Proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by the senator for Upwold in Winter 379YE, the motion sought to take advantage of an opportunity to improve the wealth of Skarsind. The ministry cost 8 wains of white granite and 2 thrones in labour, with three months needed to build it. Yargol supplied the materials and money after the Winter Solstice. Once completed, the ministry created a yearly Imperial Orc position, the Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post, appointed by the Imperial Orc senators and revocable by the Assembly of Nine, the General Assembly or the Imperial Orc National Assembly.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs gained a new yearly national title, the Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post, appointed by their senators and revocable by their National Assembly, the Assembly of Nine or the General Assembly.

t.Skarsind: The ministry was built to improve Skarsind's wealth by repairing its roads and linking it in trade with the rest of the Empire.

r.Skarsind/Southpine: The town of Torfast in Southpine became home to the completed Torfast Trading Post, with its roads repaired to enable trade.

Construct folly in Afarjasse.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by the senator for Semmerholm, the motion authorised a folly in Afarjasse, Feroz, dedicated to the region itself. It was self-funded, and the senator was permitted to build a folly of any magnitude at standard costs. After the Winter Solstice 379YE, Gant Archama provided 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns towards the work, and the folly was subsequently recorded as complete.

n.The Brass Coast: A folly celebrating Afarjasse now stands in the Brass Coast territory of Feroz, built through a self-funded Senate motion with materials and money from Gant Archama.

t.Feroz: Feroz gained a completed folly in its region of Afarjasse, paid for by 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns from Gant Archama.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Afarjasse is both the site and the dedicatee of the new folly, which was completed after Winter Solstice 379YE.

Construct mithril mine.d: The Civil Service offered two options: 100 Thrones for a six-month build producing a projected 10 wains of mithril each season, or 200 Thrones for a nine-month build producing 15 wains. The motion passed at 330 Thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Sermersuaq, and Senator Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason supplied 200 Thrones, choosing the larger mine. Unless something goes wrong, it will be complete and available for allocation at the Autumn Equinox 380YE. On completion it will create a new seat on the Imperial Bourse, and once it produces its first mithril a senator may propose a motion to allocate the seat as either National or Imperial.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Senator for Sermersuaq, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, proposed the mine and committed 200 Thrones to it, giving the nation a prospective new Bourse seat in its own lands, though whether it becomes National or Imperial will be decided by a later motion.

t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq is to gain a mithril mine projected to yield 15 wains a season, expected to be completed by the Autumn Equinox 380YE.

r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The mine is to be built at the newly discovered mithril deposit at the Face of Ikka in Suaq Fount, with construction taking nine months.

Construct shrine to Britta.d: Proposed by the Senator for Hahnmark and seconded by Reikos, the motion passed in principle and at 75 Thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Hahnmark. The Civil Service offered a modest shrine or a major one. The major option, with lodgings and spaces for meditation, prayer and religious ceremonies, was chosen: Hengest Dun supplied 18 wains of white granite and 36 crowns of labour after the Winter Solstice. The finished shrine is a significant religious structure in Kallavesa. It created a sinecure, the Watcher of Britta's Pool, which receives 9 liao and 18 votes in the Imperial Synod. By custom the title is appointed by the Wintermark national assembly from among the Winterfolk, likely for life.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a major shrine honouring its Empress Britta, and its national assembly would customarily appoint one of the Winterfolk as Watcher of Britta's Pool, likely for life, with liao and Synod votes.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa became home to a significant religious structure, a major shrine to Empress Britta able to host large numbers of pilgrims.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: The shrine was built in the Kallavesa Marsh, where Britta's regalia had been interred, providing places for pilgrims to stay, meditate, pray and hold ceremonies.

Construct the Tassato Mana Exchange.d: Proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Kahraman in Winter 379YE, the motion passed in principle and then passed at a cost of 80 thrones. The size of the ministry was left to the senator to decide, with standard costs applying. The 80 thrones were disbursed to Senator Tassato, and Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato supplied 16 wains of mithril after the Spring Equinox 380YE. The mana exchange was duly constructed in Mestra, and the new Imperial title of Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange became a League national appointment.

n.The League: The League gained a new ministry for buying mana crystals, and the Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange is appointed by the League nation.

t.Tassato: Tassato's senator proposed the ministry and Tassato's own Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato supplied the mithril, and the Mana Exchange now stands in Mestra.

Conviction.d: After the Druj were driven from Reikos and their slaves freed, Golan drew fervent crowds among the traumatised survivors. He built on the Assembly of Courage's recent judgement naming the First Empress an exemplar of Courage. The Courage assembly sent Nina of Cantiarch's Hold to preach with at least 25 liao, short of the 50 needed to refute him, and called an Inquisition on Golan for the Spring Equinox 380YE. The General Assembly passed Yael's judgement claiming she was the reborn First Empress. This inflamed matters: followers took it as support for Golan. Courage-led congregations throughout Highguard gained votes and liao, while all others lost attendance, influence and liao.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj occupation, enslavement and terror in Reikos, ended when the Black Thorns drove them out, created the despair in which Golan's preaching took hold.
n.Highguard: Highborn survivors embraced Golan's heresy, and by the end of the season every Highguard congregation led by a Courage priest was gaining votes and liao while those of other Virtues were losing both.

t.Casinea: As a Highguard territory, its Courage-led congregations shared in the swelling attendance, votes and liao, while congregations of other Virtues saw reduced influence.
t.Reikos: Freshly liberated from the Druj, Reikos was where Golan preached; Nina's under-supplied counter-campaign failed there and Yael's planned visit to its citizens only fuelled his following.

Crusade.d: The new army, proposed by Valentin of House Orzel, Senator for Weirwater, was mustering in Semmerholm amid calls to revive the Gryphon's Pride, lost in the Barrens in 276YE. The Barrens orcs had attacked the Towers of the Dawn, and troubadours urged conquest despite the orcs' legal status as foreigners. The national assembly endorsed glorious battle and crusade there, and Frederik Novarion supplied 50 liao. Dawnish units supporting the Golden Sun or defending the Towers gained a bonus; others suffered the Scorn of the Troubadours. Many nobles helped hold the Towers, but only one army joined the crusade while the Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky attacked Spiral, and the troubadours abandoned the cause.

n.Dawn: Dawn's national assembly endorsed a crusade in the Barrens, rewarding units that fought there and shaming those that did not. Pride in saving the Towers turned to dismay when only the Golden Sun joined the effort.
n.Druj: The Druj were said to have been driven back from the Barrens, leaving only the Barrens orcs between Dawn and the territory. Tales held that even the Druj feared the heart of the Forest of Peytaht, though they had moved armies through it.
n.Grendel: Rather than join the crusade, the Dawnish Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky boldly attacked Grendel-held Spiral, which the Dawnish generals evidently saw as the real priority.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named; its link is Reikos, where the Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky were stationed at the start of the season.
n.Jotun: A well-publicised agreement with the Jotun kept Dawnish armies away from the western border in favour of hero-to-hero battles beyond the Sentinel Gate, freeing Dawn's attention for the Barrens.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the war in Holberg is recalled as a time when the Druj moved armies through the Forest of Peytaht.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: a Dawnish knight warned that once Dawn became bogged down in Urizen, it would not easily get free to strike the Barrens.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn-infested depths of Brocéliande were named as one dangerous route from Reikos to Dawnguard.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: in the last months of the war in Holberg, the Druj moved their armies through the Forest of Peytaht.
t.Reikos: The Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky began the season in Reikos, from where the quickest route to the Barrens lay through the feared Forest of Peytaht.
t.Semmerholm: Dawn's fourth army was nearly mustered in Semmerholm, with nobles pressing for it to take up the banner of the Gryphon's Pride.
t.Spiral: The Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky attacked in Spiral instead of joining the Barrens crusade, and Spiral Castle was said to have admitted it was part of Dawn again.
t.The Barrens: Dawn proclaimed a crusade to conquer the Barrens, prized for the mithril of the Fangs and the weirwood of Peytaht, but only the Golden Sun joined. Its strategy of ambushes rather than open battle failed to keep the cause alive.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Valentin of House Orzel, Senator for Weirwater, proposed the fourth Dawnish army and was expected to announce its name and composition.

r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: The Barrens orcs attacked the Towers of the Dawn and the houses of Dawnguard. Many Dawnish nobles and their retinues helped hold the nearly fallen Towers through the siege.

Cuttings.d: Briars normally manifest their lineage in adulthood, occasionally in early teens, but almost never as infants. Since the Autumn Equinox eight newborns in Upwold have shown it from birth: seven in Tower March, and one to visitors from Ashill who spent three months in King's Stoke in the Spring. The children are healthy, indeed supernaturally so, age normally, and are being well cared for; one man who called them evil and urged that they be got rid of was sent home with his teeth in a sack. Speculation runs from a misplaced briar burial to the briar agitator or the risen Marcher dead. Talk of soldiers exposed to vernal curses and Rivers of Life elsewhere is largely dismissed as superstition.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj campaign is recalled as one in which potent spring curses were used by both sides in Holberg and Reikos.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's territory of Reikos is named as a place where the Druj campaign saw potent vernal curses.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: League-held Holberg is named as a territory that saw potent spring curses during the Druj campaign.
n.The Marches: Marcher families in Tower March are raising an unprecedented number of infant briars and caring for them practically. Landskeepers are investigating the cause, and locals suspect a hidden briar burial, the briar agitator or the risen Marcher dead.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan Karsk is cited as a territory where Imperial armies often fought under the influence of Rivers of Life.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is cited as a territory where Imperial armies often fought under Rivers of Life auras.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is cited as a site of potent spring curses during the Druj campaign, though any link to the births is widely derided.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk is named as a territory where Imperial armies fought under Rivers of Life.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is cited as a site of potent spring curses from both sides during the Druj campaign.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is named as a territory where Imperial armies often fought under Rivers of Life.
t.Upwold: Eight babies born in Upwold in three months showed briar lineage from birth, with every case tracing back to Tower March.

r.Upwold/Tower March: Seven of the eight briar infants were born in Tower March, around King's Stoke, and the eighth was born to visitors who had stayed there. Local landskeepers are seeking the cause of what is clearly something amiss in the region.

Declare war on the Barrens orcs.d: Proposed by Weirwater and seconded by Astolat, the motion called war the only virtuous answer to a surprise attack by a foreign nation that had reportedly slain 3000 Imperial citizens in a season and was besieging an Imperial fortification. The motion passed. The Barrens orcs lost the legal protections given to foreigners, though a delegation from them would still be protected as if they were foreigners. The attack on the Towers of Dawn halved the fortification's effective strength from 6000 to 3000. Only about a fifth of that loss was dead soldiers; the rest was damage to the structure.

n.Dawn: The senators for Weirwater and Astolat brought the motion after the Barrens orcs attacked and besieged the Towers of Dawn, halving the fortification's effective strength from 6000 to 3000.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the motion targets the orcs of the Barrens, a territory the map records as Druj-held that season.

t.The Barrens: The orcs of the Barrens became enemies of the Empire and lost the legal protection given to foreigners, though a delegation from them would still be treated as foreigners under the law.

Dying light.d: Cold sleet turning to stinging hail accompanied a supernatural despondency in Bastion, whispering that the paragons and exemplars were distant, irrelevant or mere stories. Highborn magisters identified it as Winter magic of the twentieth magnitude. Because the White City and its basilicas stand in Bastion, the curse was seen as an attack on the Imperial faith and the Synod itself. During the Winter Solstice every congregation in Bastion produced only half as much liao and half as many Synod votes, a reduction that also affected the selection of Highguard senators, including the Necropolis seat due that season, and any national Bourse title allocation. The curse faded completely by the end of the Solstice.

n.Highguard: The curse struck at the heart of Highborn faith, halving the liao and Synod votes of Bastion's congregations and weakening their priests' say in senatorial appointments and any national Bourse allocation.

t.Bastion: Bastion endured a grim winter of hail and supernatural despair that emptied temples, and its congregations provided only half their usual liao and votes until the curse faded at the end of the Winter Solstice.
t.Necropolis: The appointment of the senator for Necropolis, due that season, was affected because Bastion's congregations carried only half their usual votes in selecting Highguard senators.

Falcon in winter.d: Angry Winterfolk accused Wintermark of betraying Skarsind's traditions. Under the war hero Dogri, they entrenched themselves at Crow's Ridge, collapsed passes and destroyed a bridge, and warned the Senate and Military Council to stay out. No violence occurred, but an army sent against fellow citizens would be committing murder. The Wintermark assembly was offered two courses: urge withdrawal from Skarsind, or back those who stayed. Its judgement discouraged joining Dogri, encouraged settling in Wintermark lands and sought an amicable agreement. Withdrawal only works if Skarsind's spoils of war pass to the orcs, and the Four Seasons Market stayed in Wintermark hands. The judgement therefore had no effect.

n.Imperial Orcs: Their new homeland was challenged: Crow's Ridge was not counted under their control, and any orc entering would be supplied and sent back. They could still return a senator, but removing Dogri by force risked bloodshed and murder charges.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Dogri bitterly asks why Holberg was not given up instead, blaming its wealth and influence.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Ridge sits on the Otkodov border, and its defenders are veterans of the Thule war who refuse to submit to orcs of any kind.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Dogri asks why Karsk was not given up instead, blaming its wealth and influence.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark faced a rebellion of its own people claiming its name in Skarsind. Its assembly discouraged support for Dogri and urged resettlement, but this failed because the Four Seasons Market was never handed over.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark was named as one of the Wintermark territories where Skarsind's Winterfolk might find new homes if they withdrew. Its senator is also among those that Skarsind resource holders could still help to appoint.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Dogri resentfully asks why Holberg was not relinquished instead of Skarsind.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa was named as one of the territories where Winterfolk leaving Skarsind might resettle. Skarsind resource holders could still take part in appointing its senator.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Dogri resentfully asks why Karsk was not relinquished instead of Skarsind.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Ridge lies isolated on Skarsind's border with Otkodov.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was named as a possible new home for Winterfolk leaving Skarsind. Skarsind resource holders could still help appoint its senator.
t.Skarsind: The Winterfolk rebels split Skarsind, holding Crow's Ridge against orc settlement while disgruntled residents left their farms and mines to join them. Wintermark resources there suffered reduced production under orc rule.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Ridge lies in the south-eastern foothills of the Silver Peaks.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Dogri's followers fortified Crow's Ridge, collapsed passes and destroyed a bridge, and declared it Wintermark still. The region was not counted as Imperial Orc territory, and its defenders vowed to fight any intervention.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Mentioned in passing: any Imperial Orc entering Crow's Ridge would be supplied and sent back to Pakaanan's Pass or Skogei Glen.
r.Skarsind/Solvihill: Mentioned in passing: the Solvihill Beggarwood Barrens is listed among the Skarsind spoils of war that would need to pass to the orcs.
r.Skarsind/Southpine: Mentioned in passing: Southpine Southbound is listed among the Skarsind spoils of war that would need to pass to the orcs.

Fortify the Ore Hills.d: The motion passed in principle and at 150 Thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Upwold. Construction costs were reduced because the Empire had captured the partially built Jotun fort, so the work needed only 40 wains of white granite, 10 Thrones in labour and six months. Silas Merrick provided the white granite and the 10 Thrones after the Winter Solstice 379YE. Work began and was due to finish shortly before the Summer Solstice 380YE, provided the Empire still controlled the site.

n.Jotun: The Jotun had begun this fort in the Ore Hills and abandoned it half-built. The Empire captured it and set about finishing it as an Imperial fortification.
n.The Marches: Upwold's senator proposed the motion and received the funds. The fortification was intended to strengthen the Empire's hold on the Mournwold, a Marcher territory.

t.Mournwold: The Mournwold, then divided between the Jotun and the Marches, was to gain an Imperial fortification. It was due to be completed before the Summer Solstice 380YE if the site stayed in Imperial hands.

r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The captured, half-built Jotun fort in the Ore Hills was to be completed as The First Step over six months, using 40 wains of white granite.

Golden Trumpets.d: The trumpets sounded over the Semmerstones, in a Sarvosian theatre, at the Gate of Summer, in a quiet hall in Hahnmark, at a crossroads in Karov and in the great hall of the Lyceum. The message declared that whoever performed the greatest arcane projection, drawing on any realm, between the Winter and Summer Solstices would be named Champion of Meraud and carry his favoured staff for a year and a day. What the staff does is unknown, though it is expected to be potent and may relate to the realm of the winning ritual. Meraud cares only who performs a projection, not who devised it. The contest also offers a chance to impress, and perhaps gain the patronage of, the Summer eternal.

n.Dawn: A chorus of trumpets sounded over the Semmerstones in Dawnish lands, bringing Meraud's challenge directly to Dawn's magicians.
n.Navarr: Meraud's proclamation thundered through the great hall of the Lyceum in Navarri-held Hercynia, inviting the covens there to compete for his staff.
n.The Brass Coast: The announcement rang out at the Gate of Summer in Brass Coast territory, giving Freeborn wizards the chance to compete for the title of Champion of Meraud.
n.The League: A deafening roar of trumpets burst out in a Sarvosian theatre, carrying Meraud's challenge to the League's magicians.
n.Varushka: A terrifying explosion of sound at a crossroads in Karov delivered Meraud's challenge to Varushkan wizards.
n.Wintermark: A deafening blast of brass broke the quiet of a hall in Hahnmark, announcing Meraud's contest to Wintermark's magicians.

t.Hahnmark: Golden trumpets blasted through an otherwise quiet hall in Hahnmark, one of the Summer-linked sites where Meraud's challenge was proclaimed.
t.Hercynia: The trumpets and Meraud's proclamation resounded triumphantly in the great hall at the Lyceum in Hercynia.
t.Karov: A terrifying explosion of trumpet sound erupted at a crossroads in Karov, where the voice announced Meraud's contest.
t.Madruga: Meraud's challenge was announced at the Gate of Summer, one of the places tied to Summer magic where the trumpets sounded.
t.Sarvos: A deafening roar of golden trumpets filled a Sarvosian theatre as Meraud's challenge was proclaimed there.
t.Semmerholm: A chorus of trumpets rang out over the Semmerstones, carrying the Summer eternal's call for wizards to perform great arcane projections.

Land fit for heroes.d: Wintermark gave up Skarsind, liberated from the Thule in late 377YE, as a homeland for the Imperial Orcs in recognition of their friendship and heroic deeds. The Synod could still veto the assignment, though not the relinquishment, until the first Senate session of the Winter Solstice. If vetoed, the Senate could assign Skarsind to any nation. Otherwise the orcs moved their holdings to Skarsind with civil service help and bonesetters' savings. Orc soldiers living in the territory will elect a senator by placing weapons before candidates. That senator will appoint generals and the Advisor on Orc Affairs. The Brilliant Shore becomes an Imperial Orc national seat, and the Steel Fist's offices move to Torfast.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the offices of the Steel Fist bourse seat were relocated away from Crown's Quay to Torfast.
n.Imperial Orcs: The orcs gained Skarsind as a homeland and the right to elect a senator by a vote of their soldiers. That senator will now appoint the Summer Storm and Winter Sun generals and the Advisor on Orc Affairs, ending the old pit-fighting stop-gap. All of this still depended on the Synod not vetoing the assignment.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is noted as having been liberated from the Thule orcs in late 377YE.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark gave up its fourth territory to the Imperial Orcs, a decision not popular with everyone in the nation. The Senate was to decide whether the steinr Joakim keeps the Brilliant Shore seat until Summer 380YE or whether it passes to the orcs at once.

t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Steel Fist's offices were moved from Crown's Quay to Torfast in Skarsind.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind became the Imperial Orc homeland, with large numbers of orcs settling there over the winter. Its Brilliant Shore became an Imperial Orc national bourse seat. The assignment remained open to a Synod veto, which would halt further efforts to help the orcs claim it.

r.Skarsind/Southpine: The offices of the Steel Fist were relocated to Torfast in Southpine. Sarcophan Delves merchants are now obliged to trek there to deliver the seat's ilium, which they resent.

Long roads to ruin.d: A dozen Druj, including a coven of ghulai, crossed the Semmerlak under a flag of truce to address the Senate. They kept apart from their escort and performed daily blessings as a precaution against Imperial treachery. A small Thule party came south through Karsk without a flag of truce, citing the peace with Otkodov, and brought a bound orc prisoner over a legal matter tied to events in Hercynia. A Grendel vessel docked at Crown's Quay under truce, claiming an invitation to discuss ending the war, and seemed notably more sombre. Orcs from the Barrens emerged into northern Reikos with the heads of two dozen fleeing Stone Toad Druj and sought out the Navarr over the unhonoured peace treaty.

n.Dawn: Dawnish escorts brought word of the Druj delegation, while the Barrens orcs were unhappy to find two Dawnish armies in Reikos and quietly distrusted the Dawnish not to attack them.
n.Druj: A grim, aloof Druj delegation with ghulai travelled under truce to address the Senate on a serious matter, while two dozen Stone Toad stragglers fleeing the weirwood slave camps were killed by the Barrens orcs.
n.Grendel: A sombre Grendel representative and his "servant" arrived by ship under a flag of truce, claiming to have been invited to discuss terms to end the conflict with the Empire.
n.Highguard: The Grendel landed at Crown's Quay and were escorted to Anvil by armed guards, with the Highborn responsible for bringing word of their procession.
n.Navarr: The Barrens orcs asked to speak to their friends among the Navarr, chiefly about why the peace treaty had not been honoured, and the Navarr were to be told of their coming.
n.Thule: A confident Thule party travelled to Anvil without a flag of truce, relying on the peace between the Empire and Otkodov and bringing a bound prisoner over a legal matter to be dealt with under the treaty.
n.Varushka: Varushkan patrols in Krevsaty challenged the Thule and provided them with an escort despite their refusal of one, and were to bring word of the emissaries to Anvil.

t.Astolat: The Thule party passed through Astolat, where it became clear that one of their number was a bound prisoner.
t.Casinea: All four orc contingents were expected to come down through Casinea on their way to Anvil, and the Thule were led towards it by their Varushkan escort.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the Thule said their prisoner's presence related to a legal matter arising from recent events in Hercynia.
t.Karsk: The Thule delegation came south through Karsk and was challenged by a Varushkan patrol before being escorted onwards.
t.Necropolis: A Grendel vessel docked at Crown's Quay under a flag of truce, briefly causing panic and rumours of invasion before their peaceful intent was confirmed.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Thule cited the state of peace between the Empire and the orcs of Otkodov as their right to travel.
t.Reikos: Orcs from the Barrens emerged into northern Reikos and presented the heads of two dozen Druj to the captains of the Black Thorns, finding two Dawnish armies present.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: some speculated that the Grendel's defeat in Spiral had taught them humility.
t.The Barrens: Orcs from the Barrens made the tiring journey out to seek the Navarr, having killed Stone Toad Druj who fled north from the pyres of the weirwood slave camps.
t.The Semmerlak: The Druj delegation crossed the Semmerlak out of the Mallum under a flag of truce to begin their overland trek to Anvil.
t.Weirwater: The Thule party travelled through Weirwater with their bound prisoner on the way to Anvil.

r.Karsk/Krevsaty: A patrol on the southern borders of Krevsaty challenged the Thule delegation, whose leader sarcastically invoked the peace, and then escorted them south.
r.Necropolis/Hedrossan: The Grendel ship arrived at Crown's Quay, where the harbour-master checked their intentions and armed guards escorted their representative towards Anvil.

March on their belly.d: After the Autumn Equinox, hail, giant rats, root blight, a cyst-breeding sickness in livestock and a nasty influenza struck the Marches. Nobody starved, but farm incomes halved, food prices climbed across the Empire, army costs rose by a tenth to a fifth and natural resupply of armies, navies and fortifications fell by a fifth. The Marcher assembly chose to encourage farmers to cut the price of food sold to the Civil Service, naming Martin Orchard to coordinate with fifty liao. As a result, Marcher-owned farms, including those in Mournwold, produced half their usual coin the following season, but the status quo was expected to return by the end of the Spring Equinox.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the page only reaches Mournwold, which they held, through the Marcher-owned farms there that shared the income loss.
n.The Marches: Marcher farmers saw their incomes halved by the cursed harvest, and after their assembly chose self-sacrifice under Martin Orchard they accepted another season of half income to restore Imperial resupply by Spring.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland was one of the three territories struck by Naeve's Twisting Blight, suffering ruined crops, sick herds, vermin and influenza among its farmers.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold was among the territories hit by the curse, its fields, stores and herds damaged and its labour-force thinned by sickness.
t.Mournwold: Marcher-owned farms in Mournwold were bound by the assembly's judgement and produced only half their usual coin in the following season.
t.Upwold: Upwold suffered the curse's hail, blight, vermin and livestock sickness, and its people fell ill with influenza, leaving fewer hands to gather what harvest remained.

Price of prosperity.d: Representative Puala of the House of the People exiled the Regario agents from Zemeh. She cited Imperial contempt and the recognition of an inhuman exemplar. Sumaah now treats Imperial ships in its waters as pirates, though the Empire has not declared war in return. Work on the Sumaah embassy in Necropolis has stalled. The Commonwealth still imposes tariffs and refuses to sell artisan's oil to Imperial captains. Rigia thanked the Empire but has arranged for Jarmish slaves to arrive at the Spring Equinox. Jarm awaits formal apologies. Angered by the ban on trading Bourse resources with Asaveans, the Tarquinius family withdrew its white granite offer.

n.Highguard: Work has stalled on the Sumaah embassy under construction in Highguard's territory of Necropolis, now that Sumaah has broken off relations with the Empire.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Senator Atte of Sermersuaq is named as the person Imperial captains should approach about Commonwealth tariffs and bureaucracy.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Tarquinius family says it has found another buyer on the Bay of Catazar for its white granite, one willing to deal pragmatically with Asaveans, and Sarcophan merchant-captains remain regular visitors to the Bay's ports.
t.Necropolis: Construction of the Sumaah embassy in Necropolis has stalled following Sumaah's declaration of war, and the ambassador the Senate agreed to appoint has not yet been named.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Senator Atte of Sermersuaq is the suggested contact for Imperial captains troubled by Commonwealth tariffs.

Red star.d: Scholars grew unsure how many stars make up the Phoenix. Its magic now needs extra effort, and those attached to it suffer listlessness. Astronomancers in Urizen, Varushka and the Brass Coast reported a tiny star, possibly red, trailing the Wanderer. It is unnamed, and the Conclave might name it by Declaration of Concord. The Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri offered to build a device to study it if given 75 weltsilver and 10 crowns. It promised a grand unveiling at the Spring Equinox. Meanwhile mania spread, with afflicted magicians reported in Varushka, Dawn and the Navarr trods, and in foreign lands too.

n.Dawn: In Dawn's rose gardens, a cabal of weavers found one of their number cackling to the plants and whispering stories to the leaves. This was one of the reported cases of the spreading mania.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the story remarks that it had been a long time since the Druj threatened Zenith.
n.Urizen: Urizeni observatories were among those that spotted the new star. The Observatory of the Blazing Mirror offered to build a device to study it. Meanwhile the Spire of Twisting Shadows was overwhelmed by Urizeni mages harmed by astronomantic accidents and by a tulpa of the Phoenix.
n.Varushka: Varushkan observatories reported sighting the new star. From the dark woods came word of a volhov howling at the sky after a chance encounter on the road at night.

t.Zenith: Zenith was home to both responses to the strange skies: an Iteri observatory sought materials to examine the new star, while a healing spire in the forests struggled with a flood of maddened magicians.

r.Zenith/Iteri: Arbiter Horace's Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri offered to build a device to view the new star if given 75 weltsilver and 10 crowns. It planned a grand unveiling at the Spring Equinox for the archmages, grandmasters and its benefactor.
r.Zenith/Lustri: In Lustri's snowbound forests, Papiria's Spire of Twisting Shadows was swamped with new patients from Ankra, Caeli and Peregro. Three of them had been damaged by a tulpa of the Phoenix and would not eat, and she feared the spire would have to stop taking admissions.

Road to Bramar.d: Acting apparently in line with an agreement with Ambassador Lukash Biessek von Temeschwar, the Suranni freed nearly a hundred slaves who were former Imperial citizens or their children, mostly bought "in good faith" from unscrupulous slavers. They were brought by wagon through Feroz to Bramar. The Suranni were unapologetic about buying slaves at all, accusing the Empire of hypocrisy for trading in goods produced by slaves. They claim to have completed the conquest of Kalino, giving them their first land border with the Empire, even though the Empire had refused their offer of a treaty. They have asked to address the Senate in closed session, with the Ambassador present, citing the Empire's wars with the Jotun and Grendel. The delegates were expected at Anvil during the Winter Solstice.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni cite the Empire's war with "the bastard Grendel" as one reason they wish to discuss a treaty.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni cite the Empire's war with the Jotun as part of the situation they wish to discuss with the Senate.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast land in Feroz now borders the Iron Confederacy, and freed former Imperial slaves were brought through it to the port of Bramar, where a Suranni delegate pointedly questioned whether anyone would refuse to trade with them.

t.Feroz: A Suranni wagon train carrying nearly a hundred freed slaves travelled through Fortagenta to Bramar, where they were released, and Feroz now shares the Empire's first land border with the Iron Confederacy.
t.Kalino: The Suranni claim to have completed the conquest of Kalino, the eastern territory of the Lasambrian hills, and regard the freed slaves as having become free once they left its hills.

Summer in Winter.d: Snow fell early across the north, and isolated vales risked being cut off before Spring. More Wolves, rusalka, snow goblins and dubik were reported, along with wax-caked unliving warriors on the roads of Kamienczka. Yet a Summer enchantment urged Varushkans to seek out and challenge dark powers. Such tales often ended well, and every Varushkan with a personal resource in Varushka, including military units and fleets, gained a little extra production. Many Sovereigns mistook the season for a second Summer and stayed quiescent, leaving sacrifices unclaimed. A few grew more active instead, and new horrors may have stirred. The wise warned of overconfidence, expecting it all to end with the new year.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: there are stories that the cold crept south, bringing hail and sleet to Dawn.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page, which concerns Varushka's winter.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a land where snow is no stranger during the harsh winter.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is named among the places where the winter was harsh and snowy.
n.Varushka: Varushkans endured a brutal winter but were stirred by a Summer enchantment to face dark forces, gaining extra production from their personal resources. Many of their Sovereigns stayed quiescent, though a few grew more active and new horrors may have arisen.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that snow is no stranger to Wintermark during the harsh winter.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named. The page refers only to creatures on the northern shores of the Semmerlak and to cold spreading further south.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is named as a place where snow fell during the harsh winter.
t.Karov: Karov lay under the Summer enchantment, which drove its people to confront the dark. Stories told of unliving warriors caked in hot wax attacking travellers on its roads.
t.Karsk: Karsk was one of the four territories touched by the Summer enchantment. Wardens there might struggle to lay vengeful wraiths to rest in ruined vales and uncover treasures in the process.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova fell under the Summer enchantment, and sightings of wood-skinned dubik haunting its forests increased.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a land where snow is no stranger during the harsh winter.
