t.The Semmerlak: Tales of sinister rusalka, snow goblins and less nameable creatures haunting the Semmerlak's northern shores increased dramatically.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz suffered the harshest of the winter, so travellers to Anvil feared being unable to return before Spring. It lay under the Summer enchantment, and dubik were sighted haunting its forests.

r.Karov/Kamienczka: Stories spread of unliving warriors caked in dripping hot wax attacking travellers along the roads of Kamienczka.

Swans will sing.d: After a stalemate over the Silver Peaks, a treaty costing the Stonefield Ice Caves, and the relinquishment of Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs, Wintermark's injured pride festered over winter. The national assembly could have passed a statement of principle naming a priest to spend liao on auras of Ambition, Courage and Pride, inspiring raids into the Silver Peaks and Otkodov. Depending on the liao spent (25, 50 or 100), this would boost Wintermark businesses and military units, risk diplomatic incidents with the Thule, and possibly seize wains and ilium. The raids would be crimes under Imperial law. No judgement was passed; with Jotun concerns in Kallavesa growing, the moment passed.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: their acquisition of Skarsind is cited as one of the losses fuelling Wintermark's frustration.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the new war with the Jotun and Wintermark's fear of an invasion of Kallavesa helped the moment for raiding to pass.
n.Thule: The Thule faced possible Wintermark raids on the Silver Peaks and Otkodov in breach of the treaty, but none were sanctioned as the assembly passed no judgement.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's national assembly was offered a way to channel its wounded pride into illegal raids on the Thule for profit, but declined to pass any judgement, and the opportunity lapsed.

t.Hahnmark: Citizens with personal resources in Hahnmark would have gained a bonus from the raids, but the opportunity was not taken up.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa residents would have shared in the raiding profits, but growing concern about the Jotun threatening Kallavesa helped the moment pass.
t.Otkodov: Thule-held Otkodov, especially its south and south-west, was the proposed target of Wintermark raids, which never took place as no judgement was passed.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq, divided between Wintermark and the Thule, was the centre of the proposed raids and home to Wintermark citizens who would have profited, but nothing came of it.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's relinquishment to the Imperial Orcs is named as one of Wintermark's grievances.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Silver Peaks, contested in a stalemated battle and lost with the Stonefield Ice Caves, would have been the first target of any raids, but the assembly passed no judgement.

Tears in the rain.d: Stone Toad orcs still held out in Tamarbode and Grey Charge but were disorganised. A Druj fear miasma, anchored by hard-to-damage monoliths, blocked resettlement and would drain the treasury until it was cleared. Spring magic had eradicated the Reikos flux. The Vigilant Swan and the Great Forest weirwood groves were back in Imperial hands, giving the Senate two Bourse seats to allocate. Spoils of war awaited the Military Council. Many restless dead haunted the land, and Magister Gideon proposed a plan to deal with them. Two great works were offered: restoring the Gardens of High Chalcis and building the fortress of Exile in Broken Ride. The Senate later assigned Reikos to Highguard, and both works were commissioned.

n.Druj: The Druj lost Reikos and their citadel of Urith Barath, and their last orcs were left disorganised in Tamarbode and Grey Charge, many sheltering around the fear-exuding monoliths. Their gardens under Buruk Tepel had prospered and could teach the Empire lessons.
n.Highguard: Highborn refugees expected Reikos to be assigned to them, and the Senate did assign it to Highguard, making the Vigilant Swan a national seat. Highguard went on to commission both the Gardens of High Chalcis and the fortress of Exile, though it faced the miasma and the unquiet dead of its slaughtered people.
n.Navarr: The Navarr helped liberate Reikos: the Black Thorns under General Foxden struck north into Broken Ride fast enough to stop a massacre and free the slaves in the camps. Navarri of Peakedge Stead also wished to help restore the gardens in gratitude to the Highborn who had defended Therunin.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Bastion were among those assuming Reikos would go to Highguard, and siege engineers from the White City helped draw up the plans for Exile.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the proposed fortress of Exile would keep watch on the threat from Brocéliande to the north-east.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Casinea expected Reikos to be assigned to Highguard, and engineers from the Silent Sentinel helped present the plans for Exile.
t.Reikos: Reikos was liberated but left poisoned, haunted and blanketed in Druj miasma, which prevented resettlement and taxation. It was later assigned to Highguard, and the Gardens of High Chalcis and the fortress of Exile were commissioned to help restore it.
t.Therunin: Highborn refugees from Therunin awaited Reikos's assignment, and the people of Peakedge Stead, both Highborn and Navarri, were keen to help restore the Gardens of High Chalcis.

r.Reikos/Broken Ride: Navarr forces took the camps below the Great Forest, where many slaves fought their way free and the weirwood groves returned to Imperial hands. Broken Ride was also the chosen site for the fortress of Exile, commissioned in Winter 380YE.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: The Druj citadel of Urith Barath at High Chalcis was destroyed and the town lay in ruins, though its Druj-tended gardens survived. Those gardens were reclaimed as a great work in Summer 380YE.
r.Reikos/Grey Charge: Grey Charge remained one of the last two regions held by disorganised, defensive Druj, and Imperial forces were expected to retake it easily.
r.Reikos/Haros Water: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers found the same suffering and atrocity across Haros Water as elsewhere in Reikos.
r.Reikos/Longshire: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers reported widespread suffering and atrocity across Longshire after its liberation.
r.Reikos/Riverwatch: The Vigilant Swan in Riverwatch, haunted and defiled by Druj atrocities, was back in Imperial hands. Its white granite Bourse seat was later allocated as a national resource.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Tamarbode was one of the two western regions still held by disorganised Druj remnants, expected to fall easily to Imperial forces.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Mentioned in passing: the people of Peakedge Stead, Highborn exiles and Navarri alike, were said to be keen to help restore the Gardens of High Chalcis.

The stars aren't right.d: Bregasland and Kallavesa were protected for three months by what magicians identified as the Dripping Echoes of the Fen, curtailing Jotun raiders; an entire band of orc raiders was found drowned in southern Bregasland. A thirtieth-magnitude Night effect still concealed the northern Bay of Catazar. Drawing the Penumbral Veil shrouded Madruga (high forties), Zenith (low thirties) and Tassato (weaker), distorting their night skies, and Madruga saw a rain of harmless Sumaah frogs. Two weeks before the Winter Solstice, Thule magicians used ilium to make the Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae a permanent physical fortress in the Silver Peaks, almost certainly with the Eternal's consent, achieving about a year's construction overnight. Shroud rituals were also reclassified as shrouds rather than enchantments or curses.

n.Jotun: The marsh enchantments in Bregasland and Kallavesa were raised specifically to defend against the Jotun, curtailing their raiders, and a band of orc raiders was found drowned in southern Bregasland.
n.The Brass Coast: Madruga bore the most powerful Penumbral Veil, its night skies wildly unnatural, and a rain of harmless Sumaah frogs there gave Freeborn children new pets.
n.The League: Tassato remained under a Penumbral Veil, the weakest of the three but still impressive, frustrating any attempt to scry the territory.
n.The Marches: Bregasland's fens were guarded for three months by phantasmal protectors, quicksand and mists that spared Marchers while thwarting thieves, rustlers and orc raiders.
n.Thule: Thule magicians permanently bound the Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae into the Silver Peaks with ilium, almost certainly in collusion with the Eternal, and are already expanding it with white granite.
n.Urizen: Zenith remained shrouded by a potent Penumbral Veil in the low thirties, distorting its night skies and blocking divination.
n.Wintermark: Kallavesa's marshes were protected against the Jotun by the Dripping Echoes of the Fen, while in Sermersuaq the Thule raised a permanent fortress in the Silver Peaks.

t.Bay of Catazar: An eerie glowing fog of thirtieth magnitude still clung to the northern shores, concealing even its own nature; a powerful Eye of the High Places might examine it.
t.Bregasland: For three months the fens were protected by night magic, lost thieves were caught and an entire band of orc raiders was found drowned in southern Bregasland.
t.Kallavesa: The western Wintermark marshes shared the Dripping Echoes of the Fen protection, with phantasmal guardians aiding travellers and deterring Jotun raiders.
t.Madruga: Madruga carried the strongest Penumbral Veil, in the high forties, with extra moons, red stars and vanished skies at night, plus a rain of Sumaah frogs in autumn.
t.Sermersuaq: The Thule permanently raised the Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae, a castle of unmelting ice and adamant stone with an inhuman garrison, in Sermersuaq's Silver Peaks.
t.Tassato: Tassato's night skies were altered by the least potent of the three Penumbral Veils, which still blocks scrying of the territory.
t.Zenith: Zenith's skies showed misplaced stars and wrong moon phases under a Penumbral Veil in the low thirties.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: An overnight ritual made the Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae a permanent physical fortress on one of the highest peaks, roughly a year's construction, now being further fortified with white granite.

The worth of a life.d: With Skarsind, the Imperial Orcs held land of their own for the first time, and orcs such as those from the training camp at Estcastle moved there. Because orcs shun mining, a ministry in Gulhule (or Gildenheim) could recruit human miners from across the Empire and create an Imperial title, buying green iron, orichalcum and more at larger scales. The Fellowship of the Red Blade proposed a great work, inspired by Navarr's Memorial Gardens at Treji, to honour orcs who never saw Skarsind and share herb lore, yielding true vervain for orc herb gardens. A Torfast ministry could link trade with Temeschwar, Varushka and Hercynia, improved by matching League, Navarr and Varushkan ministries. The Senate pursued all three.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: orcs in the tale remark that Skarsind is colder than Dawn and recall their experience dealing with the Dawnish.
n.Imperial Orcs: Settling Skarsind, the orcs turned their military experience to building a homeland, gaining a ministry recruiting human miners in Gulhule, a trading post at Torfast, and a completed memorial great work tended by the Fellowship of the Red Blade.
n.Navarr: Navarr's Memorial Gardens at Treji inspired the orc memorial, and the Navarr were invited to build a matching trade ministry in the Glen of Shadows, where a trading post was begun.
n.The League: The League was offered the chance to build a ministry in Temeschwar to strengthen the Skarsind trade network, though the resolution records no such ministry being started.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: worries about the Thule are among the concerns the orcs in the tale set aside.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: an orc in the tale mentions liking their Knight's Redoubt as a reason to keep the mines productive.
n.Varushka: Varushkans, with their mining expertise, were seen as likely recruits, and Varushka was invited to build a matching trade ministry in Delev, though none is recorded as begun.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk miners already in Skarsind could be hired by the orcs, and Wintermark's past focus on trade routes into Hahnmark left Torfast's southern and western trade underdeveloped.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's trade focus from Skarsind had been on the passes into Hahnmark rather than routes south and west.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia was one of the destinations for Torfast's improved trade, and work began on a trading post in its Glen of Shadows.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov is cited as richer than Skarsind and as bordering Solvihill.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: only the orcs' Knight's Redoubt is referred to, not the territory itself.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: orcs who had lived at the main Imperial Orc training camp in Estcastle left for Skarsind.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind gained a Senate-commissioned ministry in Gulhule recruiting human miners, a trading post at Torfast, and a completed memorial great work of herb gardens for its orc settlers.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar lay on the proposed trade route south from Torfast, and a League ministry there could have enriched the network, though none is recorded as begun.

r.Hercynia/The Glen of Shadows: The Senate began work on a trading post in the Glen of Shadows, a Navarr ministry meant to widen the goods available through the Torfast crossroads.
r.Semmerholm/Estmure: Mentioned in passing: orcs from the training camp at Estcastle departed to establish a new base in Skarsind.
r.Skarsind/Estermark: Estermark's key mines were the focus of the smallest version of the miners' ministry, which would bring human labour to work them for the orcs.
r.Skarsind/Solvihill: Solvihill, bordering Karov, formed part of the proposed crossroads of the north linking Skarsind's trade eastward into Varushka.
r.Skarsind/Southpine: Southpine, bordering Temeschwar and Hercynia, was singled out by the orcs as key to the trade routes the new Torfast ministry would protect.

To sleep in Kallavesa.d: During the Autumn Equinox 379YE a contingent travelled through the Sentinel Gate to the Shrine of Britta in Necropolis and removed her armour, weapons and accoutrements. In a stormcrow ceremony these were sunk in a weirwood boat in the lake where Britta was interred in 376YE. Pilgrims now travel to Wintermark instead, so from Spring 380YE the Guardian of Britta's Shrine becomes a purely ceremonial title. The dour curse on Kallavesa's marshes abated, which mystics tentatively credit to the reunion. Britta joins the few Thrones not interred in Necropolis. The Senate chose to build a major shrine in Kallavesa Marsh and a pilgrims' trail. Work on the shrine has begun, but the trail has made no progress.

n.Highguard: Highborn helped remove Britta's relics from the Necropolis shrine. With pilgrims now going to Wintermark, the Guardian of Britta's Shrine there becomes a purely ceremonial title from Spring 380YE.
n.Wintermark: The Winterfolk laid their Empress's relics to rest beside her in the lake, and the curse on Kallavesa's marshes lifted. A major shrine is now being built in Kallavesa Marsh, its sinecure expected to be appointed by the Wintermark national assembly.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: named as the place where Emperor Barabbas's body was lost, making him another Throne not interred in Necropolis.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle is noted as interred in her family tomb in Caricomare rather than in Necropolis.
t.Kallavesa: Britta's relics were sunk in the lake at Sovvengard and the curse on the marshes abated. The Senate commissioned a major shrine, now under construction, and a pilgrims' trail on which no progress has yet been made.
t.Necropolis: Britta's relics were removed from her white granite shrine, pilgrim numbers fell sharply, and its guardianship becomes purely ceremonial from Spring 380YE.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: The Senate chose to build a major shrine to Empress Britta here, and work has begun. It is intended to house pilgrims and create a congregational sinecure with liao and Synod votes.

Trove remade.d: Probus of the Shattered Spire, Senator for Redoubt, provided a significant amount of ilium to imbue the recovered mage weapons and armour. They now resonate with the six realms in a fixed seasonal cycle following the pattern of Align the Celestial Net: day, winter, spring, night, summer, autumn, then day again. The Citadel Guard's magic quality became Cyclic Resonance. Each season the general may choose whether to use a unique order drawn from the current realm, but cannot choose which realm it is. The ilium means the cycle cannot be interrupted, reversed, delayed, skipped or shifted by magic. General Nicassia Avicia of Phoenix Reach was to decide where the cycle began. The quality was replaced by highest discipline in Autumn 383YE.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the opening vignette only alludes to orcs as the enemy the Citadel Guard faces in Spiral, and Grendel are not named.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the opening vignette shows a Navarr cambion archer, Comac, fighting alongside the Citadel Guard in Spiral and grumbling about his own poor supplies.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Citadel Guard gained the Cyclic Resonance quality, using magic drawn from the six realms in a fixed seasonal cycle. Their general, Nicassia Avicia of Phoenix Reach, was to choose where that cycle began.

t.Redoubt: The trove came from the vaulted chamber beneath the Unmade Spire in Redoubt, and Redoubt's senator, Probus of the Shattered Spire, supplied the ilium that empowered it.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the opening vignette is set among Citadel Guard sentinels and Navarr fighting in Spiral.

r.Spiral/Ateri: Mentioned in passing: in the opening vignette, the Navarr archer recalls meeting the sentinel Punam earlier in Ateri.

Vermin.d: With Holberg free, the League could field the Towerjacks again, and the League senators were expected to appoint its general. Without Old Tom's Finest, Druj-animated trees attacked Holberg's walls unopposed, though the walls stood at about two-thirds strength and the trees were expected to stop shortly before the Spring Equinox. Restoration of the Great Pits of Ennerlund continued despite flooding, with first Imperial mithril expected after Summer 380YE. Holmauer's ruins were infested by vyig and giant vermin. The Druj had dismantled the dykes holding back the Morass, which was flooding Rebeshof, raising the option of cultivating rather than containing it. Venomous briars spread through the forests of Misericorde and Utterlund where a Druj 'poison beast' had shed its venom.

n.Druj: The Druj legacy dominated Holberg: their animated trees, the dykes they dismantled, and the venomous briars sprouting where their 'poison beast' bled all plagued the territory, while scattered orc bands lingered in the northern forests as brigands avoiding Imperial troops.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Highguard-held territory of Reikos is said to be in a far worse state than Holberg.
n.The League: The League could field the Towerjacks for the first time in decades, and its senators were expected to unanimously appoint a general or risk the Senate doing so. Its people also faced the clean-up of a scarred Holberg.

t.Holberg: Holberg's walls held at around two-thirds strength against one last season of animated trees, while its mines, ruins, marshes and northern forests all bore the marks of Druj occupation, with repairs and decisions awaiting once the trees settle.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is cited as suffering a situation far more terrible than Holberg's.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Restoration of the Great Pits continued despite unexpected flooding in the lower tunnels, with first Imperial mithril expected after the Summer solstice 380YE. However, the spreading Morass and the creeping briars both threatened parts of the region.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: The ruined suburbs were becoming a lair for vyig agents, cat-sized rats and dog-sized feral cats. Any plans for the ruins had to wait until the killer trees subsided.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Venomous, unnatural briars spread through Misericorde's northern forests, where orc remnants also lurked as bandits. The briars threatened to hamper any large troop deployment.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Southern Rebeshof suffered regular flooding from the spreading Morass, with the waters subsiding less each time and risking engulfing the region. The northern briars might also reach this far south.
r.Holberg/The Morass: With the Druj having dismantled its dykes, the Morass was spreading north and sending out murderous trees. Its surprising fertility raised the option of cultivating it for herbs at the cost of farmland.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund's northern forests were overrun by poisonous briars grown where the Druj 'poison beast' shed its venom, and scattered orc bands still haunted the woods as brigands.

Whispering wind.d: Some said the wind began on the coast of Feroz, others in the mountain passes of Kahraman. Its words were always the same: Jotun in Liathaven, Lasambrians in Segura, Grendel off the coast, a hard time to be Free Born, and a good time for all hakima to talk. The speaker promised to bring olives and signed off "Cande i Riqueza". The sender was probably a Freeborn magician or coven. No hakima council had met since Britta's death, when so many hakima died that some called them a spent force. By tradition any hakima may call a council, which was private, open only to hakima and kohan. Only the Freeborn heard the words, though gossip about the wind spread widely.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the wind's message lists "Grendel off the Coast" among the challenges facing the Freeborn.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named in the message, which deals only with the Brass Coast's troubles and its hakima.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the wind's message cites "Jotun in Liathaven" as one of the threats pressing on the Brass Coast.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn hakima were called by a speaking wind to their first council since Britta's death, a test of whether these magicians remain a force in the Coast at a hard time for the Free Born.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page; the message refers only to Lasambrians in Segura and other threats to the Coast.
t.Feroz: Some said the whispering wind began in Feroz, blowing on-shore along the whole coast and carrying its message to the hakima.
t.Kahraman: Others claimed the wind came down from the mountains of Kahraman, racing through the passes to spread its call to council.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the message warns of "Jotun in Liathaven" among the dangers facing the Freeborn.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the message names "Lasambrians in Segura" as one of the challenges confronting the Brass Coast.

r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Fontargenta marked one end of the stretch of Feroz coast where the speaking wind was said to blow on-shore.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Oranseri marked the other end of the coastline along which the wind was said to blow, whispering its invitation.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Some said the wind raced down the mountain passes between Serra Briante and Serra Damata.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Serra Damata was named as one side of the mountain passes through which some said the whispering wind descended.
